The layout, the rules and the server are unchanged.
points: Light: soft diffuse light, ambient occlusion from depth, height fog that glows toward the sun, bloom, PBR Neutral tone mapping and a grade (src/render/open/post.ts).
Ground: CC0 textures over the surfaces, the palette still choosing colours; rock on steep slopes from three sides (src/render/open/ground.ts).

Models: 40 made with Meshy from concept art painted after the reference (buildings, stalls, the well, resource nodes, street props, boulders, the ten trade packs), fitted into each one's own box; about 1,000 credits.

Trees at full size with two levels of detail and blossoms by the square; crags on the cliffs; boulders; isles on the horizon; painted clouds; a hazy world tree; lit windows at night; the cog under a cream and blue sail.
Built things in vertex colours get wood, stone or plaster grain; creatures keep their colours.
Tests: tests/stress/look.spec.ts draws the same places in both looks (and from the air), times both at 1080p, and the new look at medium quality; species.spec.ts counts both looks' draws.

sessions.title: The third beta playtest
sessions.summary: Nine things found playing the deployed beta. Fixed: the strobing shore foam, ground circles under farm soil, the browser asking to leave (Ctrl was crouch, so crouch-walking pressed Ctrl+W), the planned-points badge, a portrait that changed with everything you did, and no way to learn where stone and timber come from. New: mini-games with a stake, Beacons first. The two animation items (the run, the jumping overhead slash) are left to the session reworking the animations.
points: Shore foam: the sea was one 9 km square, two triangles, and the world position the GPU worked out across them was off by metres and jumped as the camera turned, so the foam round a lagoon strobed thick and thin (worst in the new look, where the user saw it). Drawn in 50 m tiles it holds still; lines thinner than a pixel fade instead of popping (fwidth). tests/integration/sea.spec.ts.

Ground circles: farm soil is laid 5 cm over the ground and its furrows higher, so the aim circle vanished over a plot. Every plot records how high its soil and furrows stand, and circles, effect rings and the shadow under you are lifted over it, edges and all; furrows now follow the ground.

Leaving the site: Ctrl was crouch and the glider's flare, so crouch-walking pressed Ctrl+W, which no page can stop; the game asked before leaving. Crouch and flare are on C now (a press on the run slides, K still slides), Ctrl means nothing in the game and the browser's shortcuts are its own again.
Skill tree: the planned points badge stands as tall as Learn and Undo, at any UI size.
Portrait: taken from a studio of its own (src/render/studio.ts) rather than every 4 s from the world, so running, fighting, the night and the rain no longer change it.

Stone and timber: the nodes and benches were there, but nothing taught them. Two quest lessons (Brenna at the quarry, Hob in Thornwood) come before the house; gather steps count what a swing gives; the marker and the site prompt say where packs are made.

Mini-games: challenge a player with F, a stake for both, a table in the world for everyone to see, the server running the game and the money (a stake kept in the island until the game ends, both islands written together, refunds on a crash or an update). Beacons is an original hex-board card game, not Sequence: Ruina doesn't recreate existing games.

Found on the way: online the browser kept the rain the server last reported but ran its own island clock ahead with every input it predicted, so under load a shower came early on the page (the shared-weather test caught it, two minutes out). The browser now works the rain out from the world clock each step, using the same schedule as the server; the server still announces when a shower starts. The online specs also close the windows they open, so the games of earlier tests stop weighing on later ones.
Animation: the run and the jumping overhead slash were started in a track of their own, then dropped unmerged at the user's word: another session owns the animations.

sessions.title: Characters, weapons and moves for the new look
sessions.summary: The new look's people and creatures after its places: jelly slimes, the hero as a made body that walks and runs as people do, made weapons, and moves played from animation libraries, retargeted bone for bone and checked against their sources. Free assets first: AGENTS.md says to look for a free model, texture or clip before making one.
points: Slimes: glossy jelly gumdrops with a pool shadow and a face that changes with mood (src/render/creatures/jelly.ts).
Hero: a Meshy model on the hero rig (fit.ts), fingers that close round the grip, a gait measured off captured walking and running.
Weapons: Meshy's sword, club, staff and bow where the box ones were, shining with the sky's light, carried at the hip and across the back.

Moves: Quaternius' sword combo and heavy combo on the sword and club, Meshy's Triple Combo Attack as the sword's other set; retarget.ts, moves.ts, /dev/retarget.html, tests/integration/retarget.spec.ts, the retarget-animation skill.
Tools: npm run image (Gemini), tools/models/weaponprep.mjs, tools/models/clips.mjs.

sessions.title: Painted icons
sessions.summary: The user asked for the UI's low-resolution pixel images to go, keeping the Parchment & Timber look but with high-quality icons. Every icon is now painted: items, packs, vehicles, skills, places and the HUD's own, 135 in one consistent hand-painted style, sharp at any UI size.
points: Painted with Gemini (Nano Banana Pro) nine to a 2K sheet on a flat key colour, the first sheet the style reference for the rest (tools/icons/paint.mjs); tools/icons/catalog.mjs says what each icon shows and which emoji or item it stands for. 20 images in all, about $2.70, with four sheets painted again (a background not as asked, gliders painted as birds, a dragon cut off by its cell, tiles behind the icons).

Cut out by tools/icons/bake.mjs: the background keyed out from the sheet edges and from holes it shows through (between spokes, inside a ring), soft where paint fades into it, never inside an inked contour; a glow over the key keeps the hue of the paint beside it instead of turning the key's opposite. 128 px WebP, under 1 MB together. The bake fails if content names an emoji no icon stands for.

The HUD's own pixel icons (src/ui/theme/pixelIcons.ts) are gone: uiIcon(name) draws the painted heart, mana, stamina, labor, coins, seal, menu buttons, quest marks (! on offer, ? to hand in, a grey ? under way), talk bubble, lock, craft, star, book, compass and flag. Name plates show the mark itself; the maps put it on a dark disc so it stands off the ground, and the big map draws places, houses and vehicles as painted icons rather than emoji text.

Sanctuary's icon key is 🔷 (it shared 💠 with flax); a few items have pictures of their own (seed sacks by crop, saplings, the lamb, the thunderstruck log, the cottage blueprint, the Swiftwing glider). Twemoji is no longer used, so its SVGs and credit are gone.

sessions.title: An animation library for reviewing animations with Claude
sessions.summary: A place to go through every character's animations frame by frame and tell Claude what to change: notes on an animation, a stretch of frames or a frame, poses corrected by moving the bones, and a prompt made from them that carries the code's whereabouts, the numbers and the pictures. Once Claude has changed the code, the corrections stay on screen as ghosts to compare against.
points: /dev/library.html (src/library/): the hero, slimes, crowd bodies, farm animals, townsfolk and mounts, each through an adapter (subjects/) that keeps every frame of an animation so it can be scrubbed, ghosted and posed.
Pose correction: a rotation gizmo per joint, two-bone IK for hands and feet, scale for squash and stretch, undo, exact angles; kept with a picture of before and after.
Create Prompt: open notes in one prompt (prompt.ts); notes, pictures and prompts kept in reviews/animations/ by the dev server (tools/animReviews.ts).

Checking a fix: green ghosts of the corrections on their frames and a meter of how close the animation comes; tests/integration/library-review.spec.ts measures them all (degrees and centimetres) and draws the frames as they are now.
animals.ts and villagers.ts gained restartIdles(), so a model built in the library starts its idle where the last one did.

sessions.title: Goblins: the plan, concept art and the basic goblin
sessions.summary: A plan for goblin war-bands that are easy one at a time and dangerous in a group, with Gemini concept art and a search for free assets; the user chose to start with the basic goblin, built on engine parts any creature can use, with the goblin in its own folder.
points: Plan and concept art: design/goblins.md and design/goblins/ (lineup, ambush, camp, attack tells, night raid). Decisions: Thornwood camp only, no raids, captives to rescue, the agreed difficulty, the grunt to be tested with Meshy beside a free model.

Creature engine: senses, a pack step, walk/strike/throw/heal acts, conditions with arguments, missiles and flinches, in TypeScript and Rust, compared frame by frame (three goblin scenarios in tests/conformance/ai.test.ts).
The basic goblin: shared/creatures/goblin.json and src/render/creatures/goblin/, fought in the yard with ?yard&goblins=6; tests/integration/goblin.spec.ts plays its behaviours.

sessions.title: A faster suite
sessions.summary: The whole Playwright suite, the only browser check before a push to beta, took half an hour here: it ran one test at a time, and every test starts the game afresh in a new browser (about 4 s). It now runs side by side, six pages at once, and the tests that need the machine to themselves after the rest, one at a time: 12 minutes, all 366 passing.
points: playwright.config.ts: six workers; the biggest spec files spread their tests out (test.describe.configure); @gpu and @alone tests run one at a time, after the rest in a run of the whole suite, beside the rest in a run of some of it.
@alone: tests that race the clock, stopping a server under players (update.spec) or two windows of one character; update.spec warms its own Vite before its first test.

Tests that lost races under load now wait for frames: a controller press is held for two frames, the bug report's stand-in speech comes phrase after phrase, and the reporter waits up to 5 s for the frame after the press.
Why the rest of the time goes: about 4 s per test starting the game (the scene's shaders, building the island), and other checkouts' suites sharing the laptop.

sessions.title: Lanternwick rebuilt: buildings you can walk into
sessions.summary: The town rebuilt from Quaternius' Medieval Village MegaKit, every building enterable and furnished from his Fantasy Props MegaKit; 18 buildings where there were 8.
points: Plans as data (shared/buildings.json): walls as strings of 2 m modules, storeys, stairs, roof, furniture; the same plan gives the rules their walls and floors and the picture its pieces.

Rules: doorways in the walls, upper floors and stair treads as decks, upstairs walls and furniture as decks too (solid up there, walked under below), a roof to land on; baked for the server, which plays them the same (world-conformance: into the inn and up its stairs).

Drawing: the town merged into a few meshes per neighbourhood; the house you are in cut open above your storey by its vertices, its roof still casting its shadow; warm indoor light, four shared lamps that follow you, doors that swing open, hearth fires.
Camera: indoors it looks down into the room from within the walls and never slips into a house through its door.
Player cottages from the kit, stage by stage. Meshy's building models retired.
Tools: tools/models/village.mjs packs the kits; /dev/buildings.html shows each plan, cut open, with its colliders.

sessions.title: Goblin's Dread: the way in, parties and dungeon copies
sessions.summary: Concept art for the first dungeon (a goblin lair inside the Windspire, entered by gliding into its waterfall: 15 Nano Banana Pro paintings, all kept), then the way in, parties and World of Warcraft-style instances, built so you can try the glide in before the rest of the lair is planned.
points: The Windspire's waterfall: a spring by the launch deck, a slot cut in the face, a ledge behind the curtain only a glider reaches, the portal on it.
Goblin's Dread's inner grotto, solid and drawn only in a copy of it, high above the sea.
Parties: invite by name or nearby (O), the party frame, leader, kick, lead, leave.
Dungeon copies: one per party (or player), kept 30 minutes after everyone leaves; moving between games mid-connection (crates/server/src/play/spaces.rs).
Tests: tests/integration/party.spec.ts (online), tests/integration/dungeon-way-in.spec.ts, Rust unit tests for parties and spaces.

sessions.title: The first refactor: the survey, the plan and Phase 0
sessions.summary: Before the game grows further, a refactor of the whole codebase: surveyed with five explorers, planned in fourteen phases, reviewed by the user (one merge into beta at the end; developer zones and bots; the design bible as a knowledge base), and begun on branch refactor/first.
points: The survey: the tests (395, of which 104 never open a page), content (half of it still code), the rules in TypeScript and Rust (agreeing only to about a millionth), dead code, and the architecture with accounts and developer pages (every player on beta can use the developer commands).
The baseline: the whole suite passes in 10.8 minutes on six workers, each test timed (tools/tests/timings.mjs).
Binaries (models, pictures, icons, fonts, the baked island) in Git LFS, fetched by CI from a cache.
The server listens on this machine only unless asked (--listen all, set in the Docker image), so starting one never brings up a Windows prompt.
Tidied: the merged branches and worktrees, their scratch work kept in the main checkout.

sessions.title: The first refactor: test tiers, dead code, quality settings, the Admin menu
sessions.summary: Phases 1 to 4 of the refactor on branch refactor/first, with Phase 5 begun: tests in tiers that run in seconds where they can, dead code out, the toon look retired for quality settings, an Admin menu for the developer zones and pages, and a skill for finding free assets.
points: Test tiers: unit and TypeScript-against-Rust checks on Vitest (no browser), the integration tier on Playwright, stress tests before a release; npm run check after every change.
Dead code: 48 TypeScript exports, 16 Rust items and a module nothing used; knip and clippy keep it out.
The look: one look, at high (a graphics card), medium (integrated graphics) or low (software WebGL, as CI draws: haze and grade only, plainer ground and trees, a shorter view), ?quality= to choose.

Admins: ADMIN_USERS names them (on a development server everyone, unless it names someone); the Admin menu on character select, in the world and in the yard; /dev/ and /design/ answer anyone else "not found".
The /find-assets skill: free models, textures, skies, animations, sounds and effects searched and fetched with their licences and credits.
Rust: one format (rustfmt), one random generator and one set of JavaScript maths helpers, and starting an island over now rebuilds solids in the same order every time.
